explanation:
[EFFECT] Higher humidity (red dots) clearly sits on the left — the negative side — meaning humid conditions reduce predicted rentals. Lower humidity (blue dots) is associated with near-zero or slightly positive contributions. The direction is consistently negative: as humidity rises, demand is multiplied downward.
[IMPORTANCE] Humidity is the sixth-ranked feature; its effect is real and visible but smaller in spread than the top four features.

---
[RECOMMENDATION] Staffing and bike-redistribution plans should be driven primarily by the **hour of the day** — which overwhelmingly determines whether a given hour will be busy or quiet — and secondarily by **temperature**, since warm spells can substantially lift demand even in off-peak hours. Scheduling more bikes and staff during warm, mid-to-late day hours will capture the greatest share of predicted demand variation.
